correctness.rationale: All-order proof: orientation acyclicity is equivalent to nested three-bit columns; the maximal-chain inclusion-exclusion is an exact thirteen-product identity. The unsigned count is 6*4^n-6*3^n+2^n, congruent to 2 modulo 4 for n>=2. Reversal pairs force precisely the odd-weight Fourier zeros and all even-frequency values to be 2 modulo 4. Explicit frequencies attain 2 for even n and -2 for odd n. Walsh diagonalization gives the claimed exact rank and condition number. Independent topological-sort and nested-columns exhaustive enumeration, full integer Walsh transforms, per-frequency thirteen-product checks, Parseval and the histogram certificate all passed for n=2..5. Exact-integer substitutions through n=100 confirm but do not replace the all-order proof.

value.rationale: The K_{3,n} model is the first fixed three-hub infinite biclique class beyond the solved two-hub setting, and acyclic orientations are a standard natural combinatorial object. The full edge-Fourier transform and its exact minimum nonzero multiplier give a sharp worst-case stability invariant for reconstructing reversal-even signals by convolution; the parity-dependent witness construction is essential to attain the bound. The 13-product expression evaluates arbitrary edgewise signings from a fixed structural decomposition, rather than merely reproducing the known orientation count. These are complete, motivated operator-theoretic invariants and not a choice of an arbitrary finite slice.
